findings.title: Keep the merged assignment buffer out of the child environment
findings.body: Bash preserves the export attribute of an inherited `fields` variable. With `fields` exported and a harmless 150 KB command, the baseline completed silently on Linux. The candidate’s `tr`, `sed`, and `awk` all failed with `Argument list too long`, and the guard exited zero before classification. The merge guard and owner-dispatch use the same buffer.

findings.title: Bound memory before counting delimiters
findings.body: `split` allocates an array for every apostrophe before checking the 1,000-apostrophe limit. On jq 1.6, the check alone used about 103 MiB for a 2 MiB field, compared with about 16 MiB for a raw read. The merge guard and owner-dispatch can incur that allocation concurrently, exhausting a constrained worker before either reaches the intended fallback.

findings.title: Isolate fixture commits from the user’s global Git configuration
findings.body: `git_env()` preserves `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, so every fixture commit reads the developer’s global Git configuration. With `commit.gpgSign=true`, `make test-repo-gates` can prompt for a signing key or fail during setup. A global `core.hooksPath` also runs the developer’s commit hooks across the eight concurrent sandboxes.

findings.title: Verify the engine succeeds before accepting benchmark samples
findings.body: A candidate engine with a Bash syntax error passes the file-existence check. `owner-dispatch-guard.sh` suppresses the engine’s stderr, clears its failed result, and exits zero for the benchmark’s ordinary payloads. The harness accepts every sample and reports the skipped engine work as a speedup.

findings.title: Select differential fixtures using the tools that produce their output
findings.body: The fixture uses only the operating system to select hashes, while the hooks resolve utilities through `PATH`. On macOS with Homebrew GNU coreutils’ `gnubin` first, GNU `tr` replaces a multibyte session ID byte by byte. The Darwin fixture expects BSD `tr`’s result, so unchanged owner-dispatch code fails the Unicode state comparisons.

findings.title: Pin fixture regeneration to the original Git object
findings.body: `git archive 788470c` honors replacement objects, and `git_env()` strips even a caller-supplied `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS`. In a checkout with a replacement for the baseline commit, `--regenerate` hashes the replacement tree and labels the results `788470c`. Use the full commit ID with replacement lookup disabled.

findings.title: Reject timeouts before writing baseline hashes
findings.body: A timeout becomes an ordinary result dictionary. If a loaded machine times out during `--regenerate`, that timeout is saved as the expected outcome. A candidate that also times out with the same remaining state then passes the stall case despite failing its five-second deadline.

findings.title: Normalize JSON-escaped sandbox paths in hook output
findings.body: With a double quote in `TMPDIR`, a protected-edit denial contains the sandbox path with the quote escaped in JSON. `norm()` searches only for the literal path, leaving the random temporary directory name in the digest. The hook returns the correct denial, but the differential fails on every run.
